programme.title: Afghanistan and the Nature of Modern War
programme.desc: In the course's inaugural episode, begin to explore the transformation of violent conflicts between major world powers by delving into a particularly recent example: America's 20-year war in Afghanistan.

programme.title: Nightmare Scenarios of Modern War
programme.desc: The factors that explain why wars between great powers look different nowadays, and explore what future conflicts could look like between the United States and two of its major adversaries.

programme.title: The Tools of Modern Warfare
programme.desc: How five contemporary technologies-the Kalashnikov assault rifle, improvised explosive devices, guided missiles, drones, and cyber warfare-redefined the rules of battle and leveled the playing field between world powers and insurgent groups.

programme.title: From World War to Cold War
programme.desc: The series of events that followed World War II from the allied occupation of Germany to the Greek Civil War; how the Soviet Union contended with insurgencies and the beginnings of conflict between the United States and the USSR.

programme.title: Europe's Exit from Colonial Asia
programme.desc: The future of occupied Asia becomes murky after 1945; few people want to see colonial occupiers reassert their influence; zeroing in on conflicts in Indonesia, the Philippines and India to see how geopolitics in the region transform after the war.

programme.title: China's Civil War
programme.desc: As war rages on across the globe, China has to contend with civil war; exploring the war from its colonial roots to the establishment of the People's Republic of China; how the U.S.S.R. and the United States get involved in the conflict.

programme.title: The Unfinished Korean War
programme.desc: Why America fights a war in Korea; how the U.S.S.R. engages in the conflict; whether the United States could wage a limited war on the peninsula as it intends to; what to make of a war that ends not in peace, but in an armistice.

programme.title: Britain's Exit from Palestine, Malaya, and Kenya
programme.desc: After World War II, organized rebellions explode within the British Empire; investigating the conflicts that shake postwar Palestine, Kenya and Malaya; British counterinsurgency tactics; what these confrontations reveal about war and colonialism.

programme.title: The Trial of Socrates
programme.desc: Surveying some of history's greatest trials with a visit to ancient Athens; in 399 B.C., Socrates undergoes his trial for corrupting Athenians and disrespecting their gods; In the process, he lectures his jurors on the duty of seeking the truth.

programme.title: The Trial of Gaius Verres
programme.desc: To save the Roman Republic, Cicero charges Gaius Verres, a provincial governor, with crimes against the people; Cicero's Actio Secunda aims to educate the Roman public about the corruption and rot in its political system.

programme.title: Three Medieval Trials
programme.desc: Studying three strange trials from the Middle Ages; the first involves a dead pope put on trial; the second involves an accused adulterer's walk over red-hot ploughshares. The third involves a battle whose victor is vindicated as a matter of law.

programme.title: The Trial of Sir Thomas More
programme.desc: Traveling back to Westminster Hall on July 1, 1535, when Sir Thomas Moore stands on trial for his refusal to acknowledge King Henry VIII as head of the Church of England; one of England's most revered men ends up on the chopping block.

programme.title: The Trial of Giordano Bruno
programme.desc: Giordano Bruno's ideas on natural philosophy are dangerous to 16th-century thought; his execution represents a failure of the Roman Inquisition to perform its mission to admonish, not punish; the impact of this trial on another heresy case.

programme.title: The Salem Witchcraft Trials
programme.desc: According to Professor Linder, the Salem witchcraft trials illustrate the danger of drawing conclusions ahead of evidence; gaining a greater understanding of the legal basis for a travesty that accuses hundreds of people of practicing witchcraft.

programme.title: The Boston Massacre Trials
programme.desc: A harbinger of the American Revolution, the Boston Massacre trials reflect the heated partisanship of the times; the young attorney John Adams pays a price for his decision to represent the accused British soldiers and their captain.

programme.title: The Aaron Burr Conspiracy Trial
programme.desc: Learning whether politics and justice can be kept separate in great trials; considering the conspiracy trial of Aaron Burr presided over by Chief Justice John Marshall; no one in the United States, even the president, is above the law.

programme.desc: Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

programme.title: The West in the Colonial Era
programme.desc: Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

programme.title: What is a Pirate?
programme.desc: Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

programme.title: Pirate Facts and Fictions
programme.desc: Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

programme.title: America Enters the War
programme.desc: U.S. Marines arrive in June 1965 to protect a U.S. air base; the North Vietnamese Army and the southern Viet Cong guerrillas launch attacks.

programme.title: French Indochina and the Viet Minh
programme.desc: Surveying the economic exploitation and repression that defines Vietnam in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

programme.title: Prelude to War
programme.desc: Learning about the sectional controversies and clashes that ultimately set the stage for secession and war.

programme.title: The Election of 1860

programme.desc: Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

programme.title: George Washington Takes Command
programme.desc: When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

programme.title: The Tory Rebels Who Helped Save England
programme.desc: In hindsight, it may appear inevitable that Winston Churchill takes command; at the time, it seems unthinkable that Neville Chamberlain steps down; how a few brave politicians orchestrate one of the most striking political transitions in history.

programme.title: Westward the Course of Empire
programme.desc: Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

programme.title: The West in the Colonial Era
programme.desc: Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

programme.title: What is a Pirate?
programme.desc: Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

programme.title: Pirate Facts and Fictions
programme.desc: Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

programme.title: America Enters the War
programme.desc: U.S. Marines arrive in June 1965 to protect a U.S. air base; the North Vietnamese Army and the southern Viet Cong guerrillas launch attacks.

programme.title: French Indochina and the Viet Minh
programme.desc: Surveying the economic exploitation and repression that defines Vietnam in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

programme.title: Prelude to War
programme.desc: Learning about the sectional controversies and clashes that ultimately set the stage for secession and war.

programme.title: The Election of 1860
programme.desc: The presidential canvass of 1860 is the most important in U.S. history; it results in Abraham Lincoln's election as the first Republican to occupy the White House and brings sectional tensions to a head.

programme.title: The Trial of Socrates
programme.desc: Surveying some of history's greatest trials with a visit to ancient Athens; in 399 B.C., Socrates undergoes his trial for corrupting Athenians and disrespecting their gods; In the process, he lectures his jurors on the duty of seeking the truth.

programme.title: The Trial of Gaius Verres
programme.desc: To save the Roman Republic, Cicero charges Gaius Verres, a provincial governor, with crimes against the people; Cicero's Actio Secunda aims to educate the Roman public about the corruption and rot in its political system.

programme.title: America: Forged in War
programme.desc: Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

programme.title: George Washington Takes Command
programme.desc: When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

programme.title: Julia Disobeys Emperor Augustus
programme.desc: The experiences of Julia, the daughter of Caesar Augustus; a window into the way many pre-modern societies sought to control morality; Julia's life of thwarted potential; understanding what women had to overcome to make a mark on history.

programme.title: Herodias Has John the Baptist Beheaded
programme.desc: The portrayal of the John the Baptist's death as the whim of the young femme fatale Salome; why the truth is much more complicated; the story of Salome's mother, Herodias; how Herodias's hunger for power and recognition left her exiled and forgotten.

programme.title: Andrée de Jongh and the Resistance
programme.desc: When the Germans begin their rapid invasions across Europe, many ordinary citizens are stunned; Dedee de Jongh, a 23-year-old nurse, builds an escape line through Belgium and France to rescue stranded British airmen; her courage and ingenuity.

programme.title: The Tory Rebels Who Helped Save England
programme.desc: In hindsight, it may appear inevitable that Winston Churchill takes command; at the time, it seems unthinkable that Neville Chamberlain steps down; how a few brave politicians orchestrate one of the most striking political transitions in history.

programme.title: Who Are the Celts?
programme.desc: Examining and clarifying common preconceptions about Celtic identity; painting the initial brushstrokes on the canvas of a European culture most widely perceived as Scottish and Irish while promising much more.

programme.title: The Celts and the Classical World
programme.desc: Studying the earliest written records of the Celts from Italy, Greece and Spain, dating as far back as the sixth century B.C.; scholarly theories about the Celts' migration throughout Europe; the foundation of humanity's understanding of the Celts.

programme.title: Celtic Art and Artifacts
programme.desc: How archeological studies of Celtic artifacts have woven a rich tapestry of their millennia-old society; learning about war trumpets, gold necklaces and other recovered objects from around Europe; building an image of this ever-adapting culture.

programme.title: Celtic Languages in the Ancient World
programme.desc: The discovery of Celtic inscriptions on Spain's western coast; the possibility of a common language along maritime trade routes; revolutionizing studies of Celtic origins and migration; the long-standing theory of Central European Celtic origins.

programme.title: Caesar and the Gauls
programme.desc: How several centuries of combat against Celtic-controlled Gaul made northern Italy and southern France a dangerous place for the Romans; Julius Caesar's wars against the Gauls; famous figures of world history and their encounters with the Gauls.

programme.title: Celtic Religion and the Druids
programme.desc: Celtic religious beliefs in divination, reincarnation and human sacrifice; discovering the ancient religious figures known as druids, who served as holy men, soothsayers, and even lawyers; an insight into the Celtic version of the sacred.

programme.desc: With finals week ahead of them, judge Andi Oliver first summons the chefs to Wimbledon to have a look at where they could be cooking if they win. The judges are joined by guest judge Sue Barker, host of the Wimbledon coverage for more than 20 years.

programme.title: Final Fish
programme.desc: The chefs must cook their fish courses but with some exceptionally high scoring dishes in the regional heats, each chef will need to deliver perfection in order to see off the competition. The judges are joined by guest judge Tim Henman.

programme.title: Final Main
programme.desc: It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all eight chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judge Gordon Reid.

programme.title: Final Dessert
programme.desc: It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British number one and Junior Wimbledon champion.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

programme.title: North East Starter
programme.desc: Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

programme.title: North East Fish
programme.desc: After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to night shift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

programme.title: North East Main
programme.desc: Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.

programme.title: North East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

programme.title: London South East Starter
programme.desc: Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

programme.title: London South East Fish
programme.desc: The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

programme.title: London South East Main
programme.desc: Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

programme.title: London South East Dessert
programme.desc: Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.

programme.title: London South East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

programme.title: Scotland Starter
programme.desc: Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

programme.title: Scotland Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

programme.title: Scotland Main
programme.desc: Ross is hoping to impress with 'Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

programme.title: Scotland Dessert
programme.desc: Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness, and Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils, while Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: The chefs cook their mains and, following the previous day's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her 'carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat 'A Spoonful of Sugar'.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four-course menus.

programme.title: Wales Starter
programme.desc: Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his take on a traditional healing recipe, 'Mum's Flu-Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's 'A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed.

programme.title: Wales Fish
programme.desc: After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

programme.title: Wales Main
programme.desc: The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's 'Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's 'For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with 'Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

programme.title: Wales Dessert
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great-grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

programme.title: Wales Judging
programme.desc: It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

programme.title: South West Starter
programme.desc: It's the turn of three chefs representing the south-west, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time. The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their celebratory starters.

programme.title: South West Fish
programme.desc: It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X-Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

programme.title: South West Main
programme.desc: It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second-busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

programme.title: South West Dessert
programme.desc: With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an 'Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his 'An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head-to-head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

programme.title: North West Starter
programme.desc: Three chefs take to the kitchen in a bid to represent the north-west in the national final. They include Ellis Barrie, from the award-winning Marram Grass in Anglesey, Liam Simpson-Trotman, an accomplished pastry chef and co-owner of the 4 AA rosette Orwell's in Oxfordshire, and Craig Sherrington, who sharpened his skills working under top names including Eric Chavot and is now Chef Patron of Virginia House in Cumbria.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It's the fish course and the chefs are all gunning for tens. Craig pays tribute to a friend who has revolutionised hospital food in Morecambe Bay, while Liam is inspired by health advice his grandma gave him and Ellis is dedicating his dish to the staff who delivered his son Albert. With cod, mackerel, shrimp and cockles on the menu, which of the chefs will score highly?

programme.title: North West Main
programme.desc: Time for the chefs to cook their mains and the pressure is on. Craig is hoping to impress using two cuts of Dexter beef, while Liam prepares his take on a Bajan lamb stew and Ellis prepares four cuts of suckling pig. Liam meets his personal hero, Nola Ishmael OBE, who became the UK's first ever black Director of Nursing.

programme.title: North West Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the last chance for the North West chefs to impress in a bid to make it through to the regional final. Liam is cooking 'Not So Hot Toddy' in honour of a friend who works night shifts in the NHS, while Ellis' 'Worth Their Weight in Gold' is dedicated to the staff who saved his brother's life and Craig's dish 'The Missed Celebration' pays tribute to his wife with an unusual Christmas concept.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two highest scoring chefs from the week return to cook their menus again. Judging them are Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and Andi Oliver who are joined by Dr Jake Dunning MBE, an infectious disease specialist who has been recognised for his work during the West Africa Ebola epidemic.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Starter
programme.desc: Three chefs are doing battle to represent Northern Ireland. Tommy Heaney, Head Chef at the Great House Hotel in South Wales, is taken on by Shauna Froydenlund, Chef Patron at Marcus Wareing's two Michelin starred restaurant, and James Devine, the 2017 National Chef of the Year.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Fish
programme.desc: After a tense starter course, the chefs return to the kitchen to cook their fish dishes. James is making his elevated take on a fried chicken takeaway as a tribute to the NHS staff who care for his sister. Shauna is also taking inspiration from a personal connection with a tribute to staff from a facility in her hometown of Londonderry. Tommy is hoping to impress with a dish dedicated to the discovery of DNA.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main
programme.desc: With two courses down it's time for the chefs to cook their main courses. It's the battle of beef with each using the same meat in their innovative creations. Tommy also meets the first baby ever born on the NHS.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the final chance for the chefs to impress. After such a tightly fought battle all week, each is hoping to deliver a technically perfect dessert. Tommy and James are both using passion fruit in their complex dishes while Shauna is hoping to use her pastry chef training to score full marks.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs representing Northern Ireland go head-to-head. Judging as ever are Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver who are joined by Shehan Hettiaratchy, lead trauma surgeon at St Mary's Hospital who helped treat victims of the Grenfell Tower fire.

programme.title: Finals Starter
programme.desc: The winning chefs from all eight regions must battle it out for the honour of a spot on 2018's 'Feast To Say Thank You' banquet menu, celebrating 70 years of the NHS, one of Britain's most prized institutions.

programme.title: Finals Fish
programme.desc: The chefs must prepare fish courses, and after some exceptionally high-scoring dishes in the starter round, everyone is desperate to deliver perfection. Once again, the chefs present their innovative, witty and heart-warming creations.

programme.title: Finals Main
programme.desc: It's main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. Both chefs and judges alike are amazed at the high standard of cooking and an incredible number of 10s are dished out as the chefs serve up venison, rabbit, duck, beef, lamb and pork for scrutiny.

programme.title: Finals Dessert
programme.desc: It's dessert day and with just one place remaining at the banquet feast, each chef is giving everything they've got for a chance to say thank you to the heroic NHS staff. All the chefs have significantly re-worked or re-invented their desserts since the regional heats, proving that they'll do everything they can in a bid for that final winning spot.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: It's the grand finale as the winning chefs cook their dishes at a banquet for the heroes of the NHS. Having arrived at St Bartholomew's Hospital, the chefs are shown the incredible location for event, the almost three-hundred-year-old Great Hall.

programme.title: London and South East - Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Competing for the top spot are 3 new chefs to the competition representing some of the most exciting culinary talent from London, Paul Walsh, Luke Selby and Ben Marks.

programme.title: London and South East Mains and Desserts
programme.desc: The three chefs are halfway through their heat and the pressure is mounting. Only two will proceed to Friday's judging and have a chance to represent the London and the South East region at the regional finals.

programme.title: London and South East - Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London chefs must cook their four-course menus again. The chefs need to impress the formidable judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge.

programme.title: North East: Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Three chefs new to the competition compete in the North East heats. Three of the region's chefs battle it out for the top spot: Mike Carr, Samira Effa, and Tom Anglesea. The three chefs must present the menu of their careers, inspired by 50 years of British pop music.

programme.title: North East: Main and Dessert
programme.desc: The chefs are halfway through their heat and will serve up their main courses and desserts. The stakes are high, and again they are each serving a unique take on the pop music brief. Mike is confident about his northern dish, 'Rack n Roll', which puts both classic Yorkshire hogget and traditional Lancashire hotpot in the spotlight.

programme.title: North East: Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again for the judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge, one of the British pop industry's finest.

programme.title: Central Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Newcomer Kray brings an urban edge to proceedings, with a starter inspired by grime music called 'Fire in the Booth'. It combines hot sauce, veal sweetbreads and tuna belly. Returner Sabrina is compiling a dish of her favourite ingredients, including pasta and ox cheek, for her Italian inspired starter called 'My Mixtape'.

programme.title: Central Main and Dessert
programme.desc: For his main course, Ryan Simpson-Trotman is confident his dish, `The UK's Number 1', will hit the top spot with his combination of a beef pie and rump cap. Sabrina Gidda is taking inspiration from her grandad's collection of old 45s for her `Sunday Jukebox' main: pork Wellington and Black Country faggots.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Central chefs must cook their four-course menus again for judges food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge.

programme.title: North West Starter and Fish
programme.desc: Competing for a place on the banquet menu are two chefs returning to the competition for a second time, plus a supremely talented newcomer. Liam Simpson, who co-owns a high-end gastropub near Henley-on-Thames, is hoping to make it all the way after being knocked out in the heats during the 2018 competition.

programme.title: North West Main and Dessert
programme.desc: The chefs are halfway through the regional heats and, as the lowest scoring chef will be eliminated from the competition at the end of the show, the pressure is on. They start by cooking their all-important main courses, the centrepiece of the banquet menu. Michelin-starred newcomer Hrishikesh Desai is pushing himself to the limit with a complex multipart venison dish, inspired by the bands which play at the Kendal Calling music festival.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from the north-west cook their dishes head to head for a panel of expert judges, in a bid to secure themselves a place in the national finals. Will they have acted on the advice given by the veteran judge earlier in the week, and learn from their mistakes?

programme.title: Scotland Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Three of Scotland's finest chefs do battle for a chance to cook at the banquet celebrating 50 Years of Popular Music. Gordon Jones, the only newcomer, faces returners Lorna McNee and Ben Reade, who are going head-to-head for the second time.

programme.title: Scotland Main and Dessert
programme.desc: The chefs cook their mains and desserts, each battling to produce smash hit dishes that wow their veteran. For her main, Lorna is confident her lamb dish `With A Little Help From My Friends', dedicated to supportive friends, is a celebratory dish fit for the banquet.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Scottish chefs must cook their four courses again, but this time they'll need to appeal to four new palates. Food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton, broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver plus a celebrity guest judge.

programme.title: South West Starter and Fish
programme.desc: Emily Scott is the chef proprietor of Cornwall's renowned 'St Tudy Inn'. Her two rivals are from across the sea on Jersey. Joe Baker is largely self-taught, but at just 28 already running his own restaurant, 'No 10', in St Helier. A neighbouring restaurant is Michelin starred 'Samphire' where Lee Smith is head chef.

programme.title: South West Mains and Dessert
programme.desc: Emily's David Bowie-inspired dish celebrates Britain's food heroes, and she uses Cornish duck meat from her local producer that she pairs with grilled radicchio and Malbec sauce. Meanwhile, Joe has also sourced his ingredients locally.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: The chefs need to impress the esteemed judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge, one of the pop stars the banquet will celebrate. They are joined by one half of the synthpop duo The Communards, Reverend Richard Coles.

programme.title: Wales Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Tom "Westy" Westerland is a former National Chef of Wales and head chef of the Brasserie at Lucknam Park in Wiltshire. Cindy Challoner is the former head chef at prestigious teaching restaurant "The Classroom" in Cardiff. They face Andy Sheridan formerly of Sosban restaurant in Llanelli, returning to the competition for his second attempt at making it to the banquet.

programme.title: Wales Main and Dessert
programme.desc: Andy cooks venison in celebration of his favourite band, Oasis. He accompanies the loin with rhubarb and beetroot ketchup, black pudding purée, pickled beetroot and a pistachio crumb. Westy's beef dish 'The Cow Shed' is named after a former stage at the Glastonbury Festival.

programme.title: Wales Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from Wales must cook their four-course menus again. They must take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their tributes to Britain's music success.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Starter and Fish
programme.desc: The three chefs begin by cooking their starters for a surprise veteran of the competition. Chris' dish `Brixton Academy Through the Years' is his refined take on the classic lamb, post-gig junk food he ate after nights out at Brixton Academy.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main and Dessert
programme.desc: Chris is cooking his interpretation of the classic beef dish Tournedos Rossini using guinea fowl. His inspiration is Proms in the Park and the British artists who mix classical and modern music styles. Alex's dish commemorates his late brother and the song by Northern Ireland artist Donna Taggart that he associates with the difficult time of his death.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from Northern Ireland recreate their four-course menu for the esteemed judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver. There is also a guest judge: rapper Loyle Carner.

programme.title: The Finals: Starter
programme.desc: The chefs battle to get their starter course to the Abbey Road banquet and don't disappoint with dishes dedicated to everything from Tom Jones to grime. The rivals are cooking to impress Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton, and Andi Oliver.

programme.title: The Finals: Fish Course
programme.desc: Some of the finest chefs in the UK compete to cook a fish course worthy of serving at a banquet celebrating the brilliance of British popular music, held at Abbey Road Studios. Along with the show's panel of expert judges, the rivals need to impress guest judge Kanya King.

programme.title: The Finals: Main Course
programme.desc: The eight regional champions will compete to get their main courses onto the final menu of the banquet at Abbey Road Studios. They will be cooking for the judges' food critic, Matthew Fort, cook and broadcaster Andi Oliver and restaurateur, Oliver Peyton plus guest judge, former Wham! star, Andrew Ridgeley. As ever, the judges will be looking for dishes laced with star quality and a good sprinkling of rock and roll wow factor worthy of a banquet full of the music industry's finest.

programme.title: The Finals: Dessert
programme.desc: Some of the country's finest chefs compete over the final place cooking at a banquet celebrating the brilliance of British popular music, held at Abbey Road studios. Each rival will need to cook a dessert to impress a panel of expert judges, along with guest judge Peter Hook, Joy Division and New Order bassist, and pioneer of Britain's Madchester scene.

programme.title: The Finals: Banquet
programme.desc: The chefs must cook in an unfamiliar kitchen and scale up their dishes to provide the highest calibre of dining for a full banquet room of diners. Their guests are celebrities and unsung heroes who have helped create British music's unparalleled global reputation.

programme.title: Scotland Starter
programme.desc: Three of Scotland's top chefs, Jak O'Donnell, Jimmy Lee, and Graham Campbell - attempt to impress this week's veteran judge. Having missed out last year, returning finalist Jak is determined to make it to the banquet.

programme.title: Scotland Fish
programme.desc: Scottish chefs Jak O'Donnell, Jimmy Lee and Graham Campbell fight it out for the fish course. Graham is in a confident mood but returning finalist Jak and self-taught Jimmy are pushing him hard. Will the pressure prove too much for ambitious Graham?

programme.title: Scotland Main
programme.desc: Scottish chefs Jak O'Donnell, Jimmy Lee and Graham Campbell are battling to plate up a perfect main course for this week's veteran chef. Self-taught Jimmy is honouring his mum with his rendition of her Chinese beef stew.

programme.title: Scotland Dessert
programme.desc: Today it's the Scottish chefs' last chance to impress, with the dessert course. Only two can cook for the judges tomorrow, and with one chef in the lead after a triumphant main, the pressures on for the other two to plate up perfection.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Scottish chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by WI Calendar Girl Angela Baker, who will help decide which chef will go forward to the National Finals.

programme.title: South West Starter
programme.desc: Three of the south-west's finest chefs, Jude Kereama, Josh Eggleton and Dominic Chapman attempt to impress a veteran judge with their starters. As the only newcomer, Jude is determined to plate up a winning dish, but he faces stiff competition.

programme.title: South West Fish
programme.desc: The three south-west chefs fight it out for the fish course. Despite schoolboy errors during the starter, experienced Dominic is determined to get a high score on the course. But will newcomer Jude, a seafood master, overcome his nerves to plate up?

programme.title: South West Main
programme.desc: It's a battle for the main course as the three south-west chefs go head-to-head. Newcomer Jude is brimming with determination and confidence as the main course battle hits the kitchen.

programme.title: The Very Vera Show
programme.desc: Host Vera Stewart shares recipes, along with cooking and lifestyle tips, while putting a twist on many Southern classics.

programme.title: The Very Vera Show
programme.desc: Host Vera Stewart shares recipes, along with cooking and lifestyle tips, while putting a twist on many Southern classics.

programme.title: The Very Vera Show
programme.desc: Host Vera Stewart shares recipes, along with cooking and lifestyle tips, while putting a twist on many Southern classics.

programme.title: Blood Feud
programme.desc: Kahuna and Pinwheel have a disagreement over lights and boat speed at the inlet bridge.

programme.title: Reel Outlaws
programme.desc: With the quota nearly gone, all the Captains are pushing the limits. Tyler runs aground near the bridge.

programme.title: Southern Aggression
programme.desc: With the blue fin quota extended, all the crews look to take advantage, and fish hard.

programme.title: Thunder Tuna
programme.desc: Extreme weather patterns move into the Outer Banks. The Southern captains believe they have an advantage.

programme.title: The Fast and Furious
programme.desc: A top dollar fish, caught by Zack Shackleford and his young Rasta Rocket crew, might just be a game changer.

programme.title: No Backing Down
programme.desc: The Northern fleet are not going down without a fight, but the Southern fleet battles on to keep the lead.

programme.title: Miracle Fish
programme.desc: Most of the crews are getting desperate and are willing to try anything to put them on top of the leader board

programme.title: The Home Run
programme.desc: Being away from home for extended periods of time, the crews are all feeling a little homesick.

programme.title: Storm Troopers
programme.desc: With another storm moving in, Captains are realising the season could end before they achieve their objectives

programme.title: Breaking Point
programme.desc: Mistakes and mechanical issues start to wear down the northern and southern fleets.

programme.title: All Out War
programme.desc: When one last extension is added to the quota, the competition gets tighter than ever.

programme.title: Battle for the Banks
programme.desc: A championship title is on the line, along with final paychecks and local reputations.

programme.title: Clash of the Titans
programme.desc: Opening day of winter season in the Outer Banks. FV-Tuna.Com joins the Southern fleet for the first time.

programme.title: Stick 'Em
programme.desc: Captain Nick Gowitzka has long touted the greenstick. But not every captain believes it's a necessary tool.

programme.title: Family Pride
programme.desc: Captains are trying various methods to try and come in at the top of the catch board.

programme.title: Pay to Play
programme.desc: Rasta Rocket needs money to repair damage from a previous trip, and they are not the only crew with concerns.

programme.title: Fishing Up a Storm
programme.desc: The captains must choose between fight or flight when harsh conditions pummel the fleet.

programme.title: A Fish for Frenzy

programme.title: Sin ganas de cantar
programme.desc: Mía se entera de que Sabrina estará en el concierto de RBD en Monterrey y se entristece; Max llega a Puerto Vallarta y, al ver a Celina, le dice que la quiere. Roberta le dice a Mía que no permita que Sabrina le quite las ganas de cantar.

programme.title: En el hotel
programme.desc: José y Celina se asustan al ver a Javier y al enterarse de que León está en Puerto Vallarta; el concierto de RBD fue un éxito, y Mía le agradece a Roberta sus consejos; Javier le dice a León que Diego está con una chica para distraerlo.

programme.title: Miedo a morir
programme.desc: Los chicos de RBD sufren porque en el avión en el que viajan tienen unas terribles turbulencias provocadas por una tormenta.

programme.title: Disfrutando la playa
programme.desc: Los muchachos de RBD llegan a Puerto Vallarta para reunirse con los otros estudiantes del colegio. Los estudiantes conviven haciendo diversas actividades en la playa. Diego reta a Javier a una carrera en moto acuática y el ganador se queda con Rob.

programme.title: Fiesta en la playa
programme.desc: Miguel encuentra a Mía platicando con Lucca en la alberca. Giovanni consigue botellas de licor para la fiesta en la playa. Mía habla con Celina y Vico y vuelven a ser mejores amigas.

programme.title: Espiando a su exnovia
programme.desc: Antes de regresar, los alumnos hacen una última actividad en el mar. Miguel manda a Santos a investigar a Mía, pero ella se da cuenta e inventa que se acostó con Luca. Martín le confiesa sus intenciones amorosas a Carla.

programme.title: Atracción mutua
programme.desc: Miguel le exige una explicación a Mía sobre Luca. Roberta le advierte a Diego que si Mía y Miguel siguen peleando, se terminará RBD. Javier le inventa a Roberta que Diego anda diciendo que la puede tener cuando quiera.

programme.title: Declaración de amor
programme.desc: Gastón le advierte a José que no siga investigando sobre él; Javier amenaza a Diego; Roberta rechaza a Diego cuando le pide que sea su novia; Roberta es castigada por entrar al cuarto de Diego; José le dice a Gastón que ya sabe que es su tutor.

programme.title: Serenata de amor
programme.desc: Gastón niega ser el tutor de José; Diego y Miguel le llevan serenata a Mía y Roberta, pero ellas lo toman como una burla; Pilar les dice a los alumnos que su papá ya corrió a Reverte; Roberta le pide a Alma que la lleve a casa de su papá.

programme.title: Reconciliación
programme.desc: Roberta busca a Reverte para pedirle que juntos aprendan a tratarse como padre e hija. Santos le dice a Mía que la forma de demostrar amor es perdonando. Mía le pide a Rocco que persiga y grabe a su papá, porque quiere saber quién es su novia.

programme.title: Defendiendo al profesor
programme.desc: Alma lleva reporteros a la Elite y así obliga a León a no expulsar a ningún alumno y Reverte regresa al colegio; Diego le advierte a Javier que lo desenmascarará frente a Roberta; Mía discute con Franco por negarse a retirarle su apoyo a Miguel.

programme.title: Madre sin amor
programme.desc: Franco quiere confesarle a Mía que anda con Alma, pero ella no quiere que Roberta se entere. Franco le ofrece trabajo a Miguel. Alma, celosa de Reverte, le dice a Roberta que si quiere se vaya con él. Javier golpea a Diego y lo deja inconsciente.

programme.title: En el hospital
programme.desc: Roberta le dice a León que Diego se cayó solo; Javier le confiesa a Reverte que fue él quien le pegó a Diego; Sol se enfurece al descubrir que su plan para separar a Tomás y Pilar falló; José recibe un correo informándole que su tutor murió.

programme.title: Cámara oculta
programme.desc: Roberta cree que Gastón fue quien le envió el correo a José para que deje de investigar sobre él; León corre del hospital a Roberta cuando pretendía visitar a Diego; Inés y León le dicen a Javier que ingresará a un colegio acorde a su personalidad.

programme.title: Otro colegio
programme.desc: León le muestra a Diego su oficina, para que empiece a trabajar con él; una amiga de Sabrina llama a Miguel para advertirle que no tuvo relaciones sexuales con ella; Franco le dice a Alma que no se precipite al ceder la patria potestad de Roberta.

programme.title: Renuncia por amor
programme.desc: Mía se entera de que Miguel la engaña y planea su venganza. Alma va a renunciar a la patria potestad de Roberta con tal de que ella sea feliz. Franco habla con Alma y le pide que le dé tiempo a Roberta para que tome la decisión correcta.

programme.title: La huida
programme.desc: Alma está desesperada por la desaparición de Roberta; en el colegio nadie sabe nada. José y Lupita le mienten a Alma al decirle que no saben a dónde fue Roberta. Javier ayuda a Roberta a escaparse, pero al final se arrepiente.

programme.title: Verdad dolorosa
programme.desc: Roberta golpea a Sol por burlarse de ella. Alma y Martín buscan a Roberta para hablar con ella sobre su custodia. Roberta decide irse a vivir con su padre. Lola busca entre las cosas de Lupita y encuentra los papeles donde dice que ella es adoptada.

programme.title: La verdad sobre su origen
programme.desc: Roberta le ofrece a Lupita hablar con Lola para que ya no se sienta triste, pero Lola no acepta que Lupita no le haya dicho la verdad sobre su origen desde un principio. Pilar pelea con Sol por sus burlas. Lupita se reconcilia con Lola.

programme.title: La maldad de Gastón
programme.desc: Roberta pasa su primera noche en la casa de su papá. Gastón corre a Jose de la escuela y la maestra Hilda la recibe en su casa.

programme.title: El retorno
programme.desc: Sol le confiesa a Raquel que conquistará a Gastón para que olvide a Mía. Miguel y Mía se encuentran afuera del salón y le dicen a Roberta que no habrá protesta porque los descubrieron. El profesor Enrique regresa al Colegio y se encuentra con Julia.

programme.title: La ira de Gastón
programme.desc: Roberta platica con José y le dice que Gastón la odia, ella cree que fue una carga muy grande y por eso está enojado. Alma dona toda la ropa de Roberta a una casa hogar.

programme.title: Accidente fatal
programme.desc: Gastón es buscado por la policía y cree que José fue quien los llamó. Mía le pone una trampa a Sol para que deje de usar su perfume. Teo y Miguel van con la policía a casa de Gastón. Miguel quiere impedir que Gastón se vaya.

programme.title: Una gran noticia
programme.desc: Gastón se encuentra grave en el hospital y recibe la visita de Enrique, quien aprovecha para pedirle un favor. Miguel encuentra a Franco y Alma besándose, pero ellos le piden que no le diga nada a Roberta y a Mía. José tiene miedo que Gastón muera.

programme.title: Profunda tristeza
programme.desc: León investiga a Diego y se da cuenta de que le ha estado mintiendo. Sin querer, Sol descubre que Franco y Alma son novios. El director hace una junta para decidir quién ocupará el puesto de Gastón. Jose está muy triste por la muerte de Gastón.

programme.title: Decisiones
programme.desc: Diego decide salirse del grupo porque su padre no acepta que sea cantante. Los chicos tratan de convencerlo, pero él está decidido. José platica con Lola y le dice que es doloroso ser huérfana.

programme.title: Buenas noticias
programme.desc: El profesor Enrique habla con Diego y le dice que podrá viajar a la gira en Los Ángeles. Diego le cuenta a Roberta que podrá ir con ellos a la gira. Mía se entera por un mensaje anónimo que su papá sale con Alma, ella cree que todo es mentira.

programme.title: Sin padre
programme.desc: Pilar cuestiona a Tomás sobre Celeste; Roberta admira a Diego por enfrentar a su papá; León intenta que Franco y Alma no dejen ir a sus hijas al concierto; Celeste va al Elite a visitar a Giovanni; los papás de Lola le dicen la verdad de su origen.

programme.title: Tristeza infinita
programme.desc: La banda planea su gira por Los Ángeles y todos están entusiasmados. Mía pelea con Miguel en el ensayo porque está celosa de Sabrina. Franco le da permiso a Mía para irse de viaje con Miguel.

programme.title: Felicidad incompleta
programme.desc: Max le dice a Celina que está enamorado de ella. Pilar le exige a Giovanni que le explique sobre su enfermedad. Celina recibe la visita de su mamá, la cual la hace sentir mal por su sobrepeso. León decide castigar a Diego por seguir en la banda.

programme.title: La gira
programme.desc: RBD da un show en Los Ángeles, California. Alma apoya nuevos talentos musicales. Santos le manda una rosa con dedicatoria a Lupita. Gastón le escribe una carta a Luján antes de morir. RBD regresa de gira con un gran anuncio.

programme.title: Siendo honesto
programme.desc: Roberta lee la carta que dejó Gastón. Javier se sincera con Roberta para que pueda volver a confiar en él, pero ella se decepciona más y lo abofetea. Después de ver casas, Mía le dice a su papá que ya sabe sobre su relación con Alma.

programme.title: La carta del tutor
programme.desc: Miguel se alegra al descubrir que no tuvo intimidad con Sabrina. Roberta se pelea con Mía por llamar a Alma mentirosa. Madariaga le entrega a José una carta que le dejó Gastón antes de morir. Roberta se enoja con Martín y decide huir a casa de Alma.

programme.title: Palabras verdaderas
programme.desc: Mía experimenta un conflicto por la relación de Franco y Alma. Mía habla con Alma sobre la relación que tiene con su papá y le exige que no salga con él. Miguel le reclama a Sabrina por hacerle creer a Mía que pasaron la noche juntos.

programme.title: Avergonzada
programme.desc: La mamá de Celina no la deja entrar a la boda de su hermana, al igual que a Vico, porque se avergüenza de ella, pero su novio la consuela y experimentan algo que no habían hecho antes. Se alistan los permisos para grabar el disco de RBD.

programme.title: Sin amor materno
programme.desc: Se alista la grabación del disco de RBD. Roberta se pone muy triste porque extraña a Alma, pero no puede perdonarla por tanta soledad que sintió cuando era niña, así que Martín la consuela. Mía confronta a Alma y Franco frente a Roberta.

programme.title: La confesión de Roberto
programme.desc: Tras una artimaña de León, Reverte es despedido del colegio y Roberta les confiesa a sus compañeros que el profesor es su padre. Se hace una fiesta de despedida para Reverte y Miguel sufre un desmayo, es llevado al hospital y cae en estado de coma.

programme.title: En riesgo de muerte
programme.desc: Mía llora desesperada porque Miguel puede morir. León amenaza con destruir la carrera de Alma Rey si no saca a Roberta de la escuela. Raquel desenmascara las mentiras de Sol y le afirma que nunca podrá ser una top model por su estatura.

programme.title: La venganza de León
programme.desc: León influye en los directivos de la escuela para expulsar a Roberta. Diego decide dejar la banda para proteger a Roberta de su papá. Mía se siente orgullosa de Franco y le pregunta si Miguel algún día abrirá los ojos.

programme.title: La revancha
programme.desc: Roberta, Diego y Martín Reverte arman un plan para que León sea encarcelado por los fraudes que cometió, pero León los descubre y lo impide. Alma llama a León para informarle que un amigo de ella tiene información comprometedora sobre él.

programme.title: El intercambio
programme.desc: Alma le exige a León que reincorporen a Roberta y al profesor Reverte al colegio a cambio de unos papeles que lo comprometen. Madariaga informa a los muchachos que si Miguel entra en un estado crítico y despierta puede tener daño cerebral.

programme.title: Vida olvidada
programme.desc: Diego le deja en claro a León que puede cuidarse solo y no necesita de su dinero. Mía cuida a Miguel mientras se encuentra en coma, pero cuando él abre los ojos, no la reconoce. José, finalmente, lee la carta que le dejó Gastón.

programme.title: Pérdida de memoria
programme.desc: Miguel despierta del coma, pero no recuerda nada, excepto a Diego. Diego intenta ayudar a Miguel para que recuerde. Mía se altera mucho porque Miguel no la recuerda. Los alumnos comienzan a buscar universidad.

programme.title: La prueba de embarazo
programme.desc: Vico le dice a Celina que Giovanni ya sabe sobre la prueba de embarazo, algo que preocupa a Vico y Celina, ya que no quieren que nadie sepa. Marina intenta saber quién le llamó misteriosamente al hotel y llama al celular de Alma.

programme.title: Embarazo al descubierto
programme.desc: Todos se enteran de que Celina está embarazada. Alma Rey habla con la mamá de Mía y Franco se enoja por meterse en sus asuntos. Mía piensa seguir los consejos de Alma y Lupita en torno a Miguel.

programme.title: Sola y con un hijo
programme.desc: Celina no sabe qué hacer con su bebé, se siente muy sola porque Max se fue y el profesor Madariaga la aconseja. Sol se entera del embarazo, chantajea a Celina y a sus amigas. Alma no cree en las intenciones de Marina de no acercarse a Mía.

programme.title: Confusión de nombres
programme.desc: Celina asiste a su primera cita médica. Marina le pide perdón a Franco por haberlo abandonado. Miguel le pide a Mía que le ayude a recordar sobre su novia, pero él cree que su novia es Sabrina. Diego es despedido de su trabajo por culpa de su padre.

programme.title: La mentira de Franco
programme.desc: Mía no perdona a Franco por mentirle toda su vida sobre el presunto fallecimiento de su madre. Miguel no acepta hacer la rehabilitación y Franco habla con él. Javier es inculpado en el robo de tangas y calzones a las alumnas de Elite Way.

programme.title: Tratando de recordar
programme.desc: Gandía le confiesa la verdad a Madariaga sobre las amenazas de León para que aceptara entrar en sus negocios; Mía quiere localizar a su mamá, pero Franco le dice que desapareció de nuevo; Miguel le pregunta a Diego y Roberta si Mía era su novia.

programme.title: Conociendo a mamá
programme.desc: Mía pone un anuncio en el periódico para localizar a su mamá; Pascual se niega a desafiar a León por no perder su empleo; León manda a secuestrar a Diego para utilizarlo como un golpe publicitario para su campaña; Mía y Marina se encuentran.

programme.title: Como amigos
programme.desc: Roberta termina su noviazgo con Diego por aceptar los chantajes de León. Marina le explica a Mía por qué se fue. Gandía se niega a renunciar al colegio. Mía planea irse a vivir con su mamá.

programme.title: Enfrentamiento madre e hija
programme.desc: Mía le pide permiso a Franco para irse a vivir con Marina, si las cosas salen bien. Sol, bajo el nombre de Vico, le informa a la mamá de Celina que su hija está embarazada. Celina le dice a su mamá que se va a casar con Max.

programme.title: Patria potestad
programme.desc: Franco le ofrece la patria potestad de Mía a Marina. Giovanni se hace pasar por gay para engañar al papá de Javier. Roberta acepta a Colucci como la pareja de su mamá. Miguel busca hablar con Mía para reconciliarse.

programme.title: Amor por siempre
programme.desc: Mía perdona a su papá. Marina le promete a Mía salir de sus adicciones. León es detenido acusado de malos manejos. Mía le ruega a Miguel que no se vaya a Monterrey porque lo ama. Diego le dice a Roberta que la ama.

programme.title: Sé rebelde
programme.desc: Franco y Alma se casan, José les agradece aceptarla en su familia. Diego y Roberta se reconcilian. Miguel le pide a Mía que se case con él. Pascual clausura el curso. Roberta les dice a todos que RBD seguirá.

programme.title: Una mala primera impresión
programme.desc: Mía se queda sin vacaciones por hacer un striptease. Por su parte, Diego sufre un accidente por conducir ebrio. Roberta es obligada a estudiar en la Elite Way School.

programme.title: Dos nuevos ingresos
programme.desc: Roberta intenta no ser admitida en el colegio. Por su parte, Miguel deja Monterrey, y se le dificulta presentar su examen de admisión en la Elite Way School. Además, Lupita puede estudiar gracias a su tía.

programme.title: Amor a primera vista
programme.desc: Mayra ayuda a Miguel a entrar a la escuela. Miguel, Lupita y Nico hacen su examen para entrar a la escuela. Por su parte, los chicos de cuarto año se van de viaje a Vallarta.

programme.title: Amenazas y ataques

programme.title: La infamia de la verdad

programme.title: El segundo anónimo

programme.title: La ley del más fuerte

programme.title: Enfermedad fingida

programme.title: Lupita y Roberta, ¿amigas?

programme.title: Presunto acoso
programme.desc: Franco se enfurece al saber que lo culpan de acosar sexualmente a Alma y amenaza con demandarla; Pilar acusa a su padre de corrupto; Roberta insiste en entrar al grupo coreográfico; Alma recibe una llamada del abogado de Franco.

programme.title: El novio

programme.title: Engaños

programme.desc: Randy and Cody are all hands-on deck at the Raven; things are coming down to the wire with bow season just around the corner; with just over a week left they are trying to get everything wrapped up before the first bow camp.

programme.title: Where's the TV
programme.desc: With bow camp starting off strong at the Dirty Bird, Randy is feeling good about the rest of the week, until Cody decides to head into town and places a small wager with a stranger.

programme.title: 50 Acres in 5 Days
programme.desc: The boys are still at the Raven in Missouri trying to finish planting 50 acres of food plots in five days; Randy heads to the Powder River in Montana and tries to knock down his first buck of the 2025 season.

programme.title: The Journey Within - Eastern Cape of South Africa: Blue Duiker with Dogs
programme.desc: Join Mark Peterson as he continues his hunting journey through the Eastern Cape of South Africa. In this episode, Mark takes on a unique challenge: pursuing the elusive blue duiker, one of Africa's smallest & most difficult antelope species to hunt.

programme.title: Hunting Anatolian Chamois in Turkey With Mark Peterson
programme.desc: Mark Peterson heads out on a unique hunt for the rare Anatolian Chamois, a mountain dweller found in the high elevations of northern Turkey. With a storm rolling in, Mark hopes the weather will push the Chamois down from their usual heights, giving him a rare chance to track this prey across the challenging landscape.

programme.title: The Raven Project
programme.desc: The story of a true old school deer camp meeting new world management practices to take a raw piece of hunting land and develop it into whitetail Mecca.

programme.title: Brotherly Love
programme.desc: The story of a true old school deer camp meeting new world management practices to take a raw piece of hunting land and develop it into whitetail Mecca.

programme.title: Kansas Whitetails
programme.desc: Tyler Jordan heads to one of his favorite states to hunt whitetails; the Arkansas River bottoms in Kansas sprawl for miles with unlimited amounts of big buck habitat.

programme.title: Danay & Lucas DePierre
programme.desc: Watch as Danay and Lucas DePierre, an Army and Air Force husband and wife, recount how the military shaped them into the people and parents they are today.

programme.title: Argentina Golden Dorado
programme.desc: JP heads to Argentina and Don Joaquin River Lodge in search of the elusive Golden Dorado.

programme.title: Huting a Mogan
programme.desc: Tournament angler Blair Wiggins of "Addictive Fishing" continues his fishing adventures but also shares his love of everything outdoors, including hunting, cooking, beekeeping and more.

programme.title: Young Gun

programme.title: Checking Every Box

programme.title: Friendly Competition -- Part 1
programme.desc: Capt. Mike Anderson and Capt. Ryan Rickard keep track of the catch during a day in Steinhatchee, Fla.

programme.title: Lake Atlantic
programme.desc: Capt. Jason Dozier and his buddy, Cody Williams head out of Key West to fish for pelagic and dive for Spiny lobster.

programme.title: Gloucester Giant Bluefin
programme.desc: Kyle and Jeff head out onto the open ocean to fish for the giant bluefin tuna.

programme.title: Wildbound - Alabama
programme.desc: Andy goes back to his home farm in Alabama for deer and quail hunting; he makes dishes with his former "Master Chef" contestant, Alex.

programme.title: Chasing Pelagics in Big Seas Out of Key West
programme.desc: Captains Scott Walker and Steve Rodger fish out of Key West for tuna and sailfish while battling big sharks and even bigger seas.

programme.title: Islamorada Blackfins and Mahis with Capt. Scott Stoky

programme.title: Islamorada Mixed Bag
programme.desc: Captains Scott and Steve catch a mixed bag while bottom fishing off of Islamorada with Capt. Scott Stoky.

programme.title: Yellowtail and Lemons at Hawks Cay
programme.desc: Captains Scott and Steve go yellowtailing out of Hawks Cay for some tasty yellowtail snapper; Steve picks a battle with a big lemon shark.

programme.title: Reef Fishing out of Hawks Cay
programme.desc: Captains Scott and Steve bounce around the reefs of Hawks Cay, catching a wide variety of reef dwellers.

programme.title: Sailfish Season

programme.title: Road Trips: 2 Giant Bucks in 3 Days

programme.title: Tom Miranda's Namibian Black-Faced Impala Bow Hunt
programme.desc: Tom Miranda travels to Namibia to bow hunt the rare black-faced impala.

programme.title: South America Upland Slam-Entre Rios
programme.desc: Mark is wrapping up his Argentina hunt and heading to Entre Rios to track down the final two birds on his list: the Rock Pigeon and the Eared Dove. This area is home to over 10 million birds, making it a prime hunting ground with flocks of pigeons.

programme.title: Flounder to Slam
programme.desc: Meredith learns the value of the Trash Can Slam on a flounder trip with Capt. Justin that turns into a multi-species challenge.

programme.title: Dog Daze Delight
programme.desc: Capt. Justin Leake and Meredith McCord divert attention from what's not happening with the tarpon bite to using CoastMaster, light tackle and experience to find snapper success on heavily fished public spots.

programme.title: Lonestar Legends
programme.desc: Highlighting the stories and people who have made the shooting sports and hunting lifestyle a part of their lives.

programme.title: Shooting is Life
programme.desc: Highlighting the stories and people who have made the shooting sports and hunting lifestyle a part of their lives.

programme.title: Winchester Life - More Than A Medal
programme.desc: Winchester athletes Kim Rhode and Desiree Edmonds share what it takes to compete at the highest level of clay target shooting.

programme.title: Elk Frenzy! Bowhunting Elk in the Missouri River Breaks!
programme.desc: The Missouri River Breaks of Montana is an amazing place to hunt elk; Nate and Clayton both draw tags and can't wait to get to Flatwillow Creek Outfitters for what will be Clayton's first elk hunt in almost 20 years.

programme.title: Two More Turkeys Down in Mississippi!!!
programme.desc: Host and real estate agent, Slade Priest, educates on everything from purchasing and flipping hunting properties, to improving existing ones.

programme.title: Dream Season: Adam's Epic Boone and Crockett Double
programme.desc: For veteran hunter Adam Hays, last season was unlike any other. After years of pursuing trophy whitetails, he accomplished what most hunters only dream of - taking down two record-book Boone & Crockett giants in a single season.

programme.title: Wildbound -- Alaska
programme.desc: Andy and his friend Scotty take on Kodiak Island, Alaska for an adventure of salmon fishing and hunting black-tailed deer.

programme.title: The Bully

programme.title: The Muley Freak

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way - South Dakota Public Land

programme.title: The Bearded Buck - The Fastest Illinois Hunt Ever

programme.title: I Waited 12 HOURS for REDEMPTION - Being Patient for Turkeys WORKS

programme.title: 100 Lions

programme.title: First Sit in Mississippi- Austin Riley Smokes a Giant
programme.desc: The Atlanta Braves' Austin Riley will spend September and October holding it down on the hot corner in the MLB playoffs; since he can't hunt much during the early part of deer season, he usually hunts hard during December and January.

programme.title: 165 Giant Buck With a Bow

programme.title: Bowhunting Kansas

programme.title: Undertaker Hunting Sandhill Cranes- Catch Clean Cook- Ribeye of the Sky Recipe
programme.desc: WWE's Mark Calaway, aka "Undertaker," joins Realtree's David Blanton for a sandhill crane hunt in Texas. The crew put the Franchi Shotguns to work and harvested the "Ribeye of the Sky."

programme.title: Monster Buck in Nebraska; October Bow Hunting
programme.desc: Join Tyler Jordan, Brandon Sheppard and Brantley Richardson as they hit the woods in Georgia during the peak of the November rut! Then, Tyler heads to Kansas in search of big Midwestern bucks.

programme.title: Hunting Tough Alabama Turkeys; Big Gobbler Finally Breaks; Realtree Road Trips
programme.desc: Hunting across North America.

programme.title: Bow Camp 2025 at The Dirty Bird
programme.desc: Randy is getting the last food plot of the season in down at the Dirty Bird in Oklahoma. Then opening day of the 2025 bow season starts off in an unusual way for the crew. Randy smokes a Hog and Nate Has a really close call with one of the target.

programme.title: The Raven Project - Summer Prep And Randy Raven Bow Kill
programme.desc: Randy is at the Raven spraying some clover plots, trimming limbs, checking tree stand straps, and just doing some overall summertime maintenance. Fast-forward to fall and Randy is able to catch up with one of his top hit list bucks on the Raven.

programme.title: The Raven Project - Bow Camp 2025 at The Dirty Bird Part 2
programme.desc: Nate catches up with the Oklahoma buck that he had the close call with, and Cody is able to close the chapter with a buck he has been after for a few seasons.
